messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: Elevated 5xx + timeouts detected for /v1/generate on gpu-prod cluster. Error rate spike > 6% over 5m and tail latency > 1200ms. Alerts: [errors_high, latency_tail_high]. Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/xyz

sara (oncall): I’m on it. looking at grafana now. what region/services affected?

incident-bot: Affected: gpu-prod-1, gpu-prod-2. Top endpoint: /v1/generate. Top error: 502 gateway, 504 timeout, and internal 5xx from scheduler.

sara (oncall): confirming errors in logs: lots of "scheduler: queue full" and "head-of-line blocking". attaching sample log lines.

sara (oncall): ```
2026-03-14T18:22:41Z runtime scheduler[pid=2321] ERROR: enqueue failed: queue_capacity_exceeded
2026-03-14T18:22:41Z gateway[pid=448] WARN: upstream timeout after 60s for request id=abcd-1234
2026-03-14T18:22:42Z runtime scheduler[pid=2321] INFO: queue_length=1873 avg_batch_latency_ms=812
```

jin (runtime): seeing continuous batching backlog. looks like one worker pool (gpu-prod-1-a) has stalled and is causing long KV cache hold. can we drain that node?

dalia (sre): CPU/GPU metrics show one host with gpu_util stuck at 99% and oom_kill rate low. Something is stalling inside the model process maybe due to long-running requests. recommend: 1) immediately redirect new requests away from that pool, 2) reduce max_batch_size for the cluster, 3) restart the affected serving pods if safe.

sara (oncall): step 1: add temporary blacklist route for gpu-prod-1-a in routing policy. executing.

sara (oncall): ```
# add policy to route away from node
redwoodctl routing update --cluster gpu-prod --exclude-node gpu-prod-1-a --reason "incident 1765237890"
```

ops-bot: routing change applied to 2/3 routing controllers. propagation to edge ~30s.

mike (oncall-2): taking handoff from sara in 10m. @sara leave notes.

sara (oncall): current mitigation: blacklist applied. queue length dropped from 1873 -> 420 in ~45s but error rate still ~3.5%. I've also lowered max_batch_size from 32 -> 16 for gpu-prod cluster to reduce head-of-line.

sara (oncall): ```
# change batching config
redwoodctl config set --cluster gpu-prod --batch.max_size 16 --batch.max_wait_ms 20
```

incident-bot: config change accepted, rolling to routers.

jin (runtime): please patch model runtime to skip requests exceeding 45s for KV ops — we have long tail requests currently monopolizing worker threads. I can push a safe flag to enable request-timeout-kv=45s.

sara (oncall): pushed the flag to gpu-prod-2 and gpu-prod-1-b only. leaving gpu-prod-1-a blacklisted for now.

customer-success: we are seeing customer-reported timeouts for some enterprise tenants (acct: acme-inc). flagged high priority. Do we have ETA to full mitigation? need messaging.

mike (oncall-2): I’ll take over. @sara handing off: actions done — blacklist node, lowered batch size, added KV timeout flag on two pools. Queue and errors improving but not back to baseline.

mike (oncall-2): next steps: 1) scale up capacity for short-term by adding 4 spare workers in gpu-prod autoscale group, 2) initiate controlled restart of model processes on remaining pools to reclaim stuck resources, 3) enable fallback model variant with smaller memory footprint for lowest tier traffic.

mike (oncall-2): scaling now.

ops-bot: scaling event started: +4 workers to gpu-prod-autoscale-group. expected ready ~2m.

incident-bot: new workers registered with cluster gpu-prod-2. health checks passing.

jin (runtime): restarting model process on gpu-prod-1-b now (rolling restart).

sara (oncall): post-restart queue dips to ~80, tail latency down to ~220ms, error rate ~0.9%. getting closer.

customer-success: relaying to acme-inc: we are mitigating an internal scheduling backlog that caused timeouts; minimal data exposure, ETA for normal traffic is 10-15m.

mike (oncall-2): enabling fallback model variant for non-enterprise routes to reduce memory pressure.

mike (oncall-2): ```
redwoodctl model rollout --model rdx-llama-7b-quant --traffic 30% --filter tenant!=enterprise
```

ops-bot: rollout initiated.

jin (runtime): quick root-cause hypothesis: combination of an unlucky sequence-length spike from a test customer + larger-than-normal batch sizes caused a worker to get stuck on long KV operations, causing queue buildup and head-of-line blocking. Scheduler queue implementation did not preempt long-running batches quickly enough.

dalia (sre): agree. we should add preemption threshold on scheduler and per-request priority to avoid one slow request stalling the whole batch. filing follow-up postmortem tasks.

sara (oncall): monitoring for 15m after ops. if stable, we close incident and create follow-up. Current status: error rate -> 0.6%, tail latency 180ms, all blacklisted nodes drained and cordoned, rollback conditions cleared.

incident-bot: Incident 1765237890 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager silenced.

mike (oncall-2): leaving notes: actions taken summary:
- blacklisted gpu-prod-1-a
- lowered batch.max_size 32->16 cluster-wide
- applied kv-request-timeout 45s to select pools
- scaled up +4 workers temporarily
- rolled out fallback model variant to 30% non-enterprise traffic
- restarted stuck model processes (rolling)

mike (oncall-2): follow-ups (actions added to backlog):
- scheduler: implement preemption/priority for long-running batches
- improve telemetry: per-batch hold-time histogram and head-of-line detection alert
- review routing policies to more quickly isolate bad nodes
- postmortem to include timeline and customer impact (ACME incidents)

customer-success: thanks, will update customers and coordinate postmortem comms.

sara (oncall): signing off. handover complete to @mike. good job everyone. :thumbsup:

mike (oncall-2): closing thread in 20m if metrics stable.
